bibliography.note: Transactions of the American Fisheries Society 126(4): 607–621, authors Limburg, Pace, Fischer, Arend, as in the ledger.

claims.claim: white perch larvae did not select rotifers (Limburg et al. 1997, abstract)
claims.note: The abstract, which is what the paper cites, does not mention rotifers at all: it reports that Bosmina longirostris plus large copepodites and adult copepods made up 90.9 % of white perch larval diets (< 10 mm notochord length) and that selectivity for copepods was inversely related to selectivity for Bosmina. If the claim is from the full text it must be cited as such once read; as written ('abstract') it is not supported by the abstract.

claims.claim: Bosmina and copepods ~91 % of the diet below 10 mm (Hudson)
claims.note: The abstract says 90.9 % for white perch larvae < 10 mm notochord length in the Hudson River (Bosmina longirostris and large copepodite and adult copepods together); the value matches, but it rests on the abstract only, which the paper already says.

notes: OpenAlex lists the article as closed with no repository copy. Abstract values that may serve: striped bass larvae ate 97.4 % Bosmina + large copepods; peak Bosmina consumption coincided with the bloom, copepod consumption kept rising; copepod selectivity was high except where Bosmina exceeded 14 animals/L; specific consumption during and after the bloom was similar (2.58 vs 2.63 for white perch, units garbled in the abstract record). The companion paper Limburg, Pace & Arend 1999 (Fishery Bulletin, read in full) gives the same larvae's growth and mortality. The rotifer sentence in §3.6.3 should be re-sourced (e.g. to a paper that actually tested rotifer selection) or dropped until the full text is read.
